newsitem.title: USA: Champion sees disappointing results, stock drops.
newsitem.headline: Champion sees disappointing results, stock drops.

text.p: Champion Enterprises Inc., a maker of manufactured homes and buses, said Monday it expected disappointing first-quarter earnings, triggering a sell-off of its stock.
The stock fell $3.375 or more than 18 percent to $14.75 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the most active issues on volume of 2.3 million shares.

"I'm convinced this (stock decline) is a one-time event," said Jasmine Perry, an analyst at Goldman Sachs. "Investors seem to be looking for weakness in the industry, but the demand for this type of lower-end housing is fine."

The company said its Redman Indiana operations saw lower sales and income as it restructured its product line during the quarter. In addition, it had start-up expenses at two operations in Indiana and another one in Alabama.
Perry said the start-up costs were larger than the company had expected.
Champion said the level of retail activity, backed by strong consumer confidence and job creation bodes well for the year as it enters the spring retail selling season.
